topicGaps: AMSSM lists 35 basic/13 advanced ultrasound modules as free but per-video durations were not observed, so none of those hours count.
Hands-on scanning, imaging acquisition, injections, fluoroscopic procedures and sideline care require supervised training; no competence can be acquired here.
Spaulding internal schedule, case volumes and complete didactics were not public on fetched page.
Local PPE/ECG workflow, current emergency action plan and patient-specific return-to-sport require current professional context.

Two additional accessible AMSSM recordings now add a focused CPET lecture and an exercise-prescription/chronic-disease lecture. Their runtime is counted; they do not establish a learner’s ability to perform testing or make a patient-specific prescription.

The IOC REDs CAT2 framework is now supported by an authored teaching episode, but risk scoring cannot independently diagnose REDs or determine participation; physician-led multidisciplinary assessment remains necessary.

AMSSM ultrasound module runtimes remain unobserved and excluded. Conceptual teaching and source-hosted cases cannot substitute for probe handling, image acquisition, interpretation under supervision, or procedural skills.

No episode can replace direct supervised patient care, event coverage, PPE practice, procedures, longitudinal follow-up, team-based clinical judgment, or the confidential site-specific emergency plans required in accredited fellowship.

Public source coverage is uneven for some blueprint areas (including current, setting-specific pathways for less common medical conditions and local legal/return-to-sport rules). Use current governing-body and institutional sources; gaps are not claims of absence from formal fellowships.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: During exercise in warm conditions an athlete collapses and is confused. Best priority?

options.text: Rest, oral fluids, return if better.
Stop exertion, activate emergency response and initiate rapid whole-body cooling under local protocol while coordinating care.
Wait for labs before cooling.
Assume dehydration.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Suspected exertional heat stroke is time-critical; prompt recognition, stopping exertion, coordinated response and rapid cooling are core consensus principles. The short scenario does not establish diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: After head impact an athlete has symptoms concerning for concussion. Safest participation decision?

options.text: Return after brief rest if requested.
Remove from play, assess, and do not allow same-day return after suspected concussion.
Continue if no loss of consciousness.
Use a symptom score alone to clear.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Suspected concussion warrants removal and assessment; loss of consciousness is not required.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 13-year-old has focal pain near a growth plate after injury. Best reasoning?

options.text: Treat as adult muscle soreness because walking is possible.
Include physeal injury in differential and assess age, mechanism, findings, imaging/referral need.
Diagnose fracture from age alone.
Clear if one ultrasound image is normal.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Development changes differential; age alone does not diagnose injury. Select evaluation based on clinical question.
practiceQuestions.domain: Diagnosis, Management, and Epidemiology of Sports- and Exercise-Related Musculoskeletal Conditions (35%)

practiceQuestions.stem: Runner has progressive focal bone pain after training increase. Best next step?

options.text: Assume low-risk strain and continue unchanged.
Assess bone-stress differential/risk and choose evaluation, imaging or referral by suspected site and findings.
Use pain tolerance alone.
Order identical imaging in all cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Site, progression, exam, athlete risks and clinical question guide evaluation; vignette alone is not diagnosis.
practiceQuestions.domain: Diagnosis, Management, and Epidemiology of Sports- and Exercise-Related Musculoskeletal Conditions (35%)

practiceQuestions.stem: A tendon is hypoechoic longitudinally but appearance changes with probe angle. Best interpretation step?

options.text: Call tear based on first image.
Consider anisotropy; optimize beam angle/views and correlate clinically.
Ignore all ultrasound.
Recreate image in another patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Anisotropy is an ultrasound artifact; optimize technique and views.
practiceQuestions.domain: Diagnosis, Management, and Epidemiology of Sports- and Exercise-Related Musculoskeletal Conditions (35%)

practiceQuestions.stem: Athlete reports exertional syncope at PPE. How handle?

options.text: Focused clinical assessment before unrestricted participation.
Dismiss if young.
Clear after normal resting exam.
Assume dehydration.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Exertional symptom is a potential risk flag; screening is not diagnosis and a single normal observation is not enough to clear.

practiceQuestions.stem: Best return-to-sport plan after injury?

options.text: Calendar time guarantees readiness.
Integrate clinical recovery, functional progression, sport context and shared decision; do not guarantee.
Normal image always authorizes full sport.
Coach issues medical clearance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Readiness is contextual and reassessed; isolated time or imaging does not guarantee safety.
practiceQuestions.domain: Diagnosis, Management, and Epidemiology of Sports- and Exercise-Related Musculoskeletal Conditions (35%)

practiceQuestions.stem: Does completing this online course create ABPMR sports medicine board eligibility?

options.text: Yes, 36 hours suffice.
No; board-specific primary certification and required ACGME fellowship are separate requirements.
Yes, with quiz completion.
No sports medicine exam exists.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPMR requires its own criteria and accredited fellowship; a separate exam exists. Independent course provides no eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public AMSSM case image is free to view. May a course handout reproduce it?

options.text: Yes, public equals permission.
Link to source; reuse requires applicable permission even when de-identified.
Copy after removing caption.
Use as ground truth without context.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free viewing/de-identification do not grant redistribution rights. This course links and does not copy.

practiceQuestions.stem: Are Emergency Medicine applicants automatically included in the listed Spaulding primary-care fellowship?

options.text: No; Spaulding directs EM applicants to a separately named Emergency Sports Medicine Fellowship.
Yes, all clinical fellowships share eligibility.
There is no EM pathway.
The listed fellowship is research-only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The Spaulding page explicitly directs EM applicants to its separate EM Sports Medicine Fellowship.

assignment.title: Longitudinal fictional case-and-event portfolio
deliverables: Three fictional case analyses (one musculoskeletal, one medical/emergency, one adolescent/preventive) with prioritized differential, urgent alternatives, diagnostic reasoning and safe handoff/referral.
A one-page venue emergency action plan tabletop exercise with role map, EMS/access and communication contingencies; explicitly not an operational certified plan.
A PPE and shared-decision memo that distinguishes risk screening from guarantee and records guideline date.
An evidence appraisal table: source, date, target population, design/guideline authority, applicability and uncertainty.
A 10-minute oral case defense with one red-team question.
assignment.clinicalBoundary: Fictional educational scenarios only; not a patient-specific diagnosis, clinical recommendation or procedure authorization.

assessment.format: 12 unit retrieval checks; 12 original single-best-answer practice items; portfolio and case defense.
assessment.passingRule: Learner-selected formative threshold only; not validated against any certification examination, no board questions, no pass prediction. Review explanations and source updates.
assessment.rubric: Portfolio rubric above; MCQs graded for teaching discussion, not credentialing.

studyHours.plan: Transparent suggested self-study plan: 72 hours total across 12 units (3 h/unit reading/video study + 2 h case practice + 1 h retrieval/assessment). This is study time, not fellowship/clinical-training time; 36 lecture hours is a separate video floor not met by currently verified public runtime evidence.

unitMap.text: Foundations, athlete-centred care and evidence
PPE, prevention and exercise prescription
Sideline emergency systems and trauma
Concussion, neurologic and cervical emergencies
Shoulder, elbow and throwing athlete
Hand, wrist, pelvis, hip and thigh
Knee, leg, ankle and foot
Spine, bone stress, muscle and pain
Medical disorders, environment and sudden collapse
Adolescent, female athlete health, REDs and safeguarding
MSK imaging, ultrasound, procedures and rehabilitation
Team physician, event medicine, anti-doping, research and return-to-play

topicGaps: Verified accessible lecture time is 8.811944444444444 of the 36 target hours; the exact recorded-video deficit is 27.188055555555557 hours (27 h 11 m 17 s). Original authored scripts and planned target minutes do not count as external or rendered video hours.

No verified open full-length recording currently supplies broad PPE/preparticipation evaluation, cardiovascular screening limitations, exercise prescription, injury prevention, nutrition or prevention across chronic disease.

Substantial musculoskeletal gaps remain in shoulder, elbow, throwing athlete biomechanics, hand/wrist, hip/pelvis/thigh, ankle/foot, spine, bone stress, overuse, and comprehensive rehabilitation. The accessible knee recording is a focused traumatic-knee lecture, not regional coverage of the whole blueprint.

No verified full-length open lecture fills the MSK imaging/ultrasound competence sequence, image-selection and interpretation limits, or supervised procedures. ACGME requirements and the member-gated 35-module AMSSM ultrasound didactics page do not themselves supply open recordings.

Concussion coverage is incomplete: one verified return-after-injury lecture is not a full concussion assessment, differential, mental-health, school, rehabilitation and clinician-supervised return curriculum.

Medical-condition coverage is selective: open videos cover collapse, heat, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, hematology, eye trauma and pelvic-floor dysfunction, but not the full blueprint breadth (including asthma/allergy, diabetes, infection/mono, GI/renal, dermatology, pharmacology, psychiatry, cardiovascular conditions and pediatric issues).

Event medicine, comprehensive emergency action-plan design/rehearsal, mass participation logistics, anti-doping/TUE, safeguarding, adolescent care and REDs need further recorded instruction. The 2023 IOC consensus is a linked reading, not a video.

Twelve original public YouTube candidates from the initial packet still have unknown duration and/or unverified free full-play access; they remain excluded from totals. Do not infer runtimes from titles, transcripts, or search listings.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardStatus: A separate sports-medicine CAQ/certification examination exists for the primary-care sports medicine pathway; each sponsoring/qualifying board sets its own eligibility and maintenance requirements. ABOS separately administers the orthopaedic sports medicine subspecialty exam. Fellowship completion is not certification and does not itself establish board eligibility.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Johns Hopkins program page specifically states completion of an ACGME-accredited PM&R residency for this fellowship. ACGME 2026 program requirements generally identify prior residencies in EM, FM, IM, ONMM, pediatrics or PM&R and contain a limited exception; do not infer that this particular Hopkins program accepts all ACGME-eligible paths. Verify current program and each certifying board. ABOS applies to the distinct orthopaedic pathway.

officialProgrammes.name: Sports Medicine Fellowship Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Directory: ACGME accredited, one year; multidisciplinary comprehensive sports/MSK training; co-sponsored by PM&R and Orthopaedic Surgery. Detailed program page describes PM&R-sponsored 12-month clinical fellowship, two approved positions, ACGME accreditation, program-specific PM&R-residency eligibility, clinical exposure including pediatric/adult sports, MSK ultrasound, orthopaedic rotations, athletic/event coverage, concussion, MSK radiology and weekly didactics. Directory department grouping/co-sponsorship does not make this an orthopaedic-surgery sports fellowship; page does not publish the full lecture archive or total didactic hours.

officialProgrammes.name: Sports Medicine Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official directory-listed institutional variant; a full internal rotation or lecture curriculum was not verified in the directory discovery.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One actual physician clinical fellowship variant verified: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine PM&R Sports Medicine Fellowship. Institutional directory generic “Sports Medicine Fellowship Program” is the same program, not a second specialty. Co-sponsorship/orthopaedic rotations do not equal orthopaedic sports fellowship. The ABOS orthopaedic subspecialty pathway is a distinct neighboring board pathway, not another Hopkins variant. Not a research-only postdoc, sports science degree, athletic training program, or non-physician supplement. No pediatric-only Hopkins All Children’s fellowship added from a search-result YouTube video: it is a separate program requiring verification, not an institutional variant in the provided packet.
sourceCaveats: Primary institutional pages verify only public program summary; they do not expose full internal curricula, full didactic archive or total programme hours.
ACGME 2026 requirements are dated/effective; re-check at enrollment. Specific Hopkins eligibility is narrower than generic ACGME entry categories.
Board exam domains and pathways differ; ABFM 2026 blueprint weights are not a proxy for every cosponsor/qualifying board’s blueprint. ABOS distinct pathway described separately.

One search-result video advertised a Johns Hopkins All Children’s pediatric fellowship; this was not added as a confirmed institutional variant because no official program page was verified in this task.

No counted videos: metadata extraction failed and direct public free playback/runtimes were not verified. Hours are unknown rather than zero-length; reported verified external hours are 0, target 36, exact gap 36 hours.

topicGaps: Verified accessible lecture time is 8.811944444444444 of the 36 target hours; the exact recorded-video deficit is 27.188055555555557 hours (27 h 11 m 17 s). Original authored scripts and planned target minutes do not count as external or rendered video hours.

No verified open full-length recording currently supplies broad PPE/preparticipation evaluation, cardiovascular screening limitations, exercise prescription, injury prevention, nutrition or prevention across chronic disease.

Substantial musculoskeletal gaps remain in shoulder, elbow, throwing athlete biomechanics, hand/wrist, hip/pelvis/thigh, ankle/foot, spine, bone stress, overuse, and comprehensive rehabilitation. The accessible knee recording is a focused traumatic-knee lecture, not regional coverage of the whole blueprint.

No verified full-length open lecture fills the MSK imaging/ultrasound competence sequence, image-selection and interpretation limits, or supervised procedures. ACGME requirements and the member-gated 35-module AMSSM ultrasound didactics page do not themselves supply open recordings.

Concussion coverage is incomplete: one verified return-after-injury lecture is not a full concussion assessment, differential, mental-health, school, rehabilitation and clinician-supervised return curriculum.

Medical-condition coverage is selective: open videos cover collapse, heat, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, hematology, eye trauma and pelvic-floor dysfunction, but not the full blueprint breadth (including asthma/allergy, diabetes, infection/mono, GI/renal, dermatology, pharmacology, psychiatry, cardiovascular conditions and pediatric issues).

Event medicine, comprehensive emergency action-plan design/rehearsal, mass participation logistics, anti-doping/TUE, safeguarding, adolescent care and REDs need further recorded instruction. The 2023 IOC consensus is a linked reading, not a video.

Twelve original public YouTube candidates from the initial packet still have unknown duration and/or unverified free full-play access; they remain excluded from totals. Do not infer runtimes from titles, transcripts, or search listings.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 17-year-old collapses during a hot practice, is confused and ataxic. What is the immediate priority?

options.text: Move to shade and observe
Suspect exertional heat stroke, activate emergency response and initiate rapid whole-body cooling while arranging transport
Give oral fluids and resume when improved
Wait for a temperature after transport

practiceQuestions.rationale: Central nervous system dysfunction with exertional hyperthermia is a medical emergency; rapid cooling is critical and should not wait for transport when on-site protocols permit.

practiceQuestions.stem: A player has suspected concussion and wants to re-enter after brief symptom improvement. Best response?

options.text: Return if a teammate watches
No same-day clearance based on symptom improvement alone; remove, evaluate and follow applicable clinical protocol
One sprint test clears return
Helmet replacement clears risk

practiceQuestions.rationale: Suspected concussion requires removal and assessment; return is clinician-directed and stepwise, not a sideline symptom-only clearance.

practiceQuestions.stem: In CDC’s six-step progression, when may the athlete advance?

options.text: After 12 hours
Only if no new symptoms at current step; each step typically minimum 24 h and provider supervision/approval
Only when coach approves
Immediately after symptoms stop

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC states provider approval/supervision, no new symptoms before advancement, typically at least 24 h per step.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABFM Medical conditions / CDC return to sport

practiceQuestions.stem: An asymptomatic athlete asks if a normal PPE guarantees absence of sudden cardiac arrest. Best counseling?

options.text: Yes, normal screening excludes it
No screening strategy eliminates risk; interpret history/exam and any tests in context and explain limitations
Universal ECG ensures zero risk
Family history is irrelevant

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening informs risk assessment but cannot guarantee future safety; apply current policy and shared decision-making, evaluate concerning findings.

practiceQuestions.stem: A youth athlete has focal bone pain that worsens with impact and persists at rest. The appropriate initial reasoning?

options.text: Assume muscle strain and continue loading
Consider bone stress injury and red flags, modify impact pending evaluation and select imaging based on clinical question
Order MRI for every athlete with pain
Clear if radiograph normal

practiceQuestions.rationale: Bone stress injury is a meaningful differential; normal early radiographs do not reliably exclude it. Clinical review and appropriate imaging/referral are needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Point-of-care MSK ultrasound shows a tendon abnormality. Which statement is safest?

options.text: Image alone establishes symptoms and causality
Interpret with history/exam; ultrasound is operator-dependent and abnormality may be incidental
All abnormalities require injection
Ultrasound replaces radiographs in every injury

practiceQuestions.rationale: Imaging findings require clinical correlation; technical quality, operator skill, and incidental findings constrain inference.

practiceQuestions.stem: During a mass-participation event, the most essential pre-event physician preparation is:

options.text: Have one physician at the finish line only
A written emergency action plan with roles, communications, transport and EMS coordination adapted to course hazards
Rely on athletes to call for help
Focus only on dehydration

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME expects event planning/implementation and EMS coordination; systems and access/transport must be planned.

practiceQuestions.stem: An athlete taking a prescribed medicine asks whether it is prohibited. Best action?

options.text: Assume legal prescription is exempt
Check the current governing-body prohibited list and sport/jurisdiction rules; use the applicable TUE process if indicated
Stop medication abruptly
Rely on old list

practiceQuestions.rationale: Prohibited status depends on current list, route/dose and applicable sport rules; never advise abrupt cessation; coordinate prescriber and TUE authority.

practiceQuestions.stem: A runner with exertional collapse is confused and very hot. Which finding changes urgency most?

options.text: Mild thirst
Central nervous system dysfunction
Sweat present
Young age

practiceQuestions.rationale: CNS dysfunction is a key warning sign for exertional heat stroke, an emergency needing immediate action.

practiceQuestions.stem: A young athlete with fatigue, recurrent injury, weight concern and menstrual change requires:

options.text: Single diagnosis from one feature
Assessment for low energy availability/REDs and differential including other medical causes, with multidisciplinary evaluation as appropriate
Immediate sport ban in all cases without evaluation
Calorie prescription from coach

practiceQuestions.rationale: Patterns may raise concern for REDs but are not independently diagnostic; careful medical assessment and multidisciplinary care are appropriate.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pathway best describes the Hopkins Sports Medicine fellowship listed on its public page?

options.text: Orthopaedic surgery sports fellowship leading directly to ABOS certificate
12-month ACGME-accredited PM&R-sponsored clinical fellowship; its stated application criterion is ACGME PM&R residency completion
Research-only non-physician course
Pediatric sports-only program

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hopkins program page specifies PM&R sponsorship, 12 months, ACGME accreditation and PM&R residency eligibility; directory co-sponsorship with orthopaedics does not reclassify it as orthopaedic fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes sports medicine board pathways?

options.text: All physicians take a single board regardless of primary specialty
Primary-care sports CAQ is board-specific (ABFM-administered and cosponsored by ABEM/ABP/ABPMR, with ABIM qualifying); orthopaedic sports medicine has separate ABOS pathway/exam
ACGME accreditation itself certifies board status
Finishing a fellowship guarantees eligibility/pass

practiceQuestions.rationale: Board pathway eligibility and certification requirements are administered by the relevant boards; fellowship completion alone is not certification. Orthopaedic sports certification is separate.

assignment.title: Longitudinal fictional case formulation, treatment-options memo and evidence update
deliverables: Use a fictional case (no identifiable or copied patient record/image) and state known facts, unknowns and assumptions.

assignment.passRule: For formative self-study only: target 80% rubric performance and remediate missed concepts against current sources. This is not a validated board predictor or credential.

assessment.format: Formative quizzes, case formulations, source appraisal, reflective communication exercise and capstone assignment.
assessment.blueprint: Use exact ABPM Addiction Medicine domains and target weights published in outline: 25% definitions/genetics/PK-PD/pharmacology/neurobiology; 20% epidemiology/trends/prevention; 40% screening/assessment/brief intervention, treatment, intoxication/withdrawal, pharmacologic and behavioral intervention, medical/psychiatric comorbidity and pain; 15% ethical/legal/liability. Substance target ranges include alcohol 15–20%, nicotine 15–20%, opioids 10–15%, sedatives/stimulants/cannabinoids each 7–10%, and lower ranges for several less prevalent classes. Ranges describe exam blueprint, not clinical importance; do not calculate additive coverage as if ranges were a quota.
assessment.limitations: Original educational questions are not official board questions and are not validated. No pass prediction.

unitMap.text: Concepts, definitions, neuroscience and the biopsychosocial model
coveredTopics: Differentiate substance use, risky use, DSM-5-TR SUD, intoxication, withdrawal, remission and recovery without conflating them.
Explain reward learning, reinforcement, neuroadaptation and vulnerability using a biopsychosocial formulation.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Epidemiology, prevention, stigma and population health
coveredTopics: Interpret prevalence, incidence, overdose trends and limitations of surveillance.
Design a prevention or screening response that accounts for structural determinants and avoids stigma.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Screening, assessment, DSM criteria and case formulation
coveredTopics: Select appropriate screening/assessment tools and explain their limits; screening is not diagnosis.
Construct a biopsychosocial differential including severity, co-occurring illness, readiness/goals, withdrawal risk and recovery environment.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Motivational interviewing, brief intervention and behavioral care
coveredTopics: Use open questions, affirmations, reflections, summaries and collaborative goal-setting.
Distinguish MI from confrontation and match psychosocial services to person goals without making them a precondition for MOUD.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Opioid use disorder, medications, overdose and linkage
coveredTopics: Compare buprenorphine, methadone and naltrexone mechanisms, indications, constraints and initiation considerations using current sources.
Plan overdose prevention/naloxone education and continuity linkage; distinguish withdrawal-only care from ongoing treatment.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Alcohol use disorder and withdrawal
coveredTopics: Differentiate acute intoxication, withdrawal syndromes and other medical/psychiatric causes of altered mental status.
Use ASAM guideline to reason about level of care and connect withdrawal management with longitudinal AUD treatment.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Sedatives, stimulants, cannabis and other drugs
coveredTopics: Compare substance-specific intoxication/withdrawal patterns and evidence-supported care without assuming one protocol applies to all.
Summarize relative blueprint emphasis including lower-frequency hallucinogens, dissociatives, inhalants, anabolic steroids and behavioral addictions.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Tobacco/nicotine, vaping and behavior change
coveredTopics: Assess nicotine use and readiness; distinguish dependence from other substance diagnoses.
Compare behavioral support and approved cessation pharmacotherapy using current FDA labeling and patient preference.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Pain, prescribed medications and co-occurring medical illness
coveredTopics: Formulate care where pain, opioid therapy, SUD and medical comorbidity intersect without punitive assumptions.
Use medication reconciliation/PDMP concepts, interactions and risk mitigation; distinguish pain-prescribing guidance from OUD treatment guidance.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Psychiatric comorbidity, pregnancy, adolescents and lifespan
coveredTopics: Recognize psychiatric/medical comorbidity and avoid attributing every symptom to use or withdrawal.
Discuss developmental, pregnancy, postpartum and adolescent contexts, family-centered care, confidentiality and safeguarding with current sources.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Ethics, law, confidentiality, equity and systems of care
coveredTopics: Identify legal/ethical issues (confidentiality, consent, capacity, mandated reporting, controlled prescribing) requiring current local policy/legal counsel.
Map transitions across inpatient, outpatient, OTP, harm reduction and community services without claiming availability.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

unitMap.text: Evidence appraisal, quality improvement and board-style synthesis
coveredTopics: Appraise study design, absolute versus relative effects, confounding and guideline currency.
Integrate board outline breadth and explain why exam preparation does not establish competency or board eligibility.
Prerequisite: physician-level biomedical knowledge and foundational clinical interviewing; for nonphysician learners, content remains educational and is not scope-of-practice authorization.

topicGaps: Only 0.873 of the 36 target video hours are supported by a unique, free public recording with observed runtime and sufficiently verified playback; 35.127 hours remain.
Verified coverage is narrow: one 52:22 Stanford CME recording on buprenorphine formulations, OUD, and pain. It does not cover the full addiction-medicine blueprint or replace supervised training.

Foundations and population health, formal assessment, MI/behavioral care, alcohol withdrawal/AUD, stimulant/sedative/cannabis and other substance-specific care, nicotine cessation, pregnancy/adolescents, ethics/law, systems and evidence appraisal remain materially under-covered by verified recordings.

A CDC overview and a Scripps alcohol-neurobiology lecture have observed runtimes but were excluded because the retrieved public player stated video unavailable. Several public candidates have no reliable observed runtime and remain uncredited.
No institutional fellows’ lecture archive or proprietary didactics are represented as open recordings. Human clinical review has not been performed.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Preventive Medicine (ABPM) — Addiction Medicine subspecialty certification examination
American Osteopathic Board of Preventive Medicine (AOBPM) — Addiction Medicine certification (separate osteopathic board pathway; verify current eligibility and exam requirements directly)
medical.boardStatus: Addiction Medicine is a physician subspecialty with a separately administered ABPM subspecialty certification exam (200 questions; four one-hour blocks; 4.5 hours including tutorial and break). ABPM ACGME-fellowship pathway requires at least 12 months in an ACGME-accredited Addiction Medicine fellowship and completion of all accredited years if longer; also requires qualifying medical degree, unrestricted current license, and current primary specialty certification. ACGME programme completion is not itself board certification. AOBPM also lists an osteopathic certification pathway; no equivalence or individual eligibility is implied. AOBPM/American Osteopathic Conjoint Examination Committee separately administers an osteopathic subspecialty certification exam; its public process page lists fellowship-completion and clinical-pathway eligibility routes subject to current board policies.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This course does not establish eligibility. ABPM requirements apply to individual applicants, including current primary specialty certification, qualifying medical degree and unrestricted license; only the board determines eligibility. Verify current ABPM/AOBPM rules and application cycle. No promise of exam readiness or passing.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Official Johns Hopkins listing verifies the institutional offering and explicitly states ACGME accreditation. CHA publicly describes its Mary Cassesso clinical fellowship and curriculum and is listed as a Harvard Medical School teaching hospital; the CHA page reviewed did not state accreditation. Preserve the institutional variants rather than treating one listing as proof of the other. These are clinical physician fellowship programmes, not research-only postdoctoral positions, generic directory categories or non-physician supplements. No institutional lecture archive has been assumed available.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins page explicitly says ACGME Accredited; CHA programme page gives detailed clinical curriculum but the page reviewed does not itself document ACGME status. Verify current ACGME ADS before making an accreditation claim about CHA.
ABPM is the explicit allopathic board authority cited here. AOBPM has a distinct osteopathic pathway; its current details must be verified directly and are not inferred from ABPM.
ABPM board blueprint is an exam scope/weighting document, not an official course syllabus, clinical protocol or predictor of passing.
ACGME requirements and milestones apply to accredited supervised fellowship education. They do not convert this course to accredited training.
Sources are date-checked 2026-10-07. Clinical pages may change; verify current guideline, label, jurisdictional law and local policy at point of use.
Human clinical review has not been performed. Independent education grants no affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, procedure competence or certification.

topicGaps: Only 0.873 of the 36 target video hours are supported by a unique, free public recording with observed runtime and sufficiently verified playback; 35.127 hours remain.
Verified coverage is narrow: one 52:22 Stanford CME recording on buprenorphine formulations, OUD, and pain. It does not cover the full addiction-medicine blueprint or replace supervised training.

Foundations and population health, formal assessment, MI/behavioral care, alcohol withdrawal/AUD, stimulant/sedative/cannabis and other substance-specific care, nicotine cessation, pregnancy/adolescents, ethics/law, systems and evidence appraisal remain materially under-covered by verified recordings.

A CDC overview and a Scripps alcohol-neurobiology lecture have observed runtimes but were excluded because the retrieved public player stated video unavailable. Several public candidates have no reliable observed runtime and remain uncredited.
No institutional fellows’ lecture archive or proprietary didactics are represented as open recordings. Human clinical review has not been performed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient presents for routine care and screens positive for unhealthy alcohol use. What is the best next conceptual step?

options.text: Treat the screening result as a confirmed severe AUD diagnosis
Discuss results and proceed to a fuller assessment using diagnostic criteria and patient context
Immediately prescribe withdrawal medication
Discharge from care because the screen predicts nonadherence

practiceQuestions.rationale: A positive screen identifies a need for further assessment; it is not itself a diagnosis or severity determination. Use person-first, nonpunitive engagement.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with opioid use disorder asks for treatment but declines counseling today. Which principle is best supported by CDC’s OUD treatment page?

options.text: Delay medications until counseling is completed
Offer or arrange MOUD and assess/referral psychosocial needs without making counseling a prerequisite
Provide detoxification alone as definitive treatment
Require abstinence from all substances before treatment

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC states offer/arrange evidence-based medication treatment; psychosocial needs should be assessed and referral offered but lack/decline should not preclude or delay MOUD.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which set contains the three FDA-approved medications for OUD named by CDC?

options.text: Buprenorphine, methadone, naltrexone
Naloxone, clonidine, disulfiram
Acamprosate, buprenorphine, varenicline
Methadone, benzodiazepine, gabapentin

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC identifies buprenorphine, methadone and naltrexone as FDA-approved medications indicated for OUD; agent selection and initiation require individualized current clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: In an educational question, which mechanism best characterizes buprenorphine for OUD?

options.text: Mu-opioid receptor partial agonist
Pure opioid antagonist
GABA-A positive allosteric modulator
Dopamine transporter blocker

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC describes buprenorphine as a mu-opioid receptor partial agonist; this mechanism fact alone does not determine a patient-specific initiation plan.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner says successful alcohol withdrawal management alone cures alcohol use disorder. Which response best aligns with ASAM?

options.text: Correct: withdrawal management is a component of initiating/engaging in AUD treatment, not a discrete definitive treatment
Correct only for inpatient cases
Correct only if withdrawal scores normalize
Incorrect only for patients with liver disease

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASAM states withdrawal management alone is not effective treatment for AUD and should be integrated into ongoing care engagement.

practiceQuestions.stem: ABPM's published Addiction Medicine content outline groups the largest overall share of questions under which umbrella?

options.text: Screening/assessment, treatment, withdrawal, pharmacologic and behavioral interventions, comorbid disorders and pain
Ethics/legal only
Neuroscience only
Epidemiology only

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPM outline assigns 40% to the listed clinical assessment/treatment group, versus 25% definitions/neurobiology/pharmacology, 20% epidemiology/prevention and 15% ethics/legal/liability.

practiceQuestions.stem: A person with OUD has experienced a nonfatal overdose. Which additional measure is specifically named by CDC?

options.text: Offer naloxone and education to the person and household/significant others
Require a written abstinence contract before referral
Use detox alone and defer follow-up
Withhold care until toxicology is negative

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC recommends offering naloxone and education to patients with OUD and household/significant others, alongside evidence-based treatment and linkage.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the CHA programme is directly supported by its public page?

options.text: One-year fellowship; lists applicants from FM, IM, OB, pediatrics and EM
Its public page confirms ABPM board eligibility for every applicant
It is a research-only postdoctoral job
It awards board certification on completion

practiceQuestions.rationale: CHA calls it a one-year fellowship and names those applicant backgrounds. Certification eligibility belongs to the board and individual pathway requirements, not a programme webpage.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description accurately characterizes the ABPM Addiction Medicine certification exam?

options.text: Separate subspecialty exam listed as 200 questions in four one-hour blocks; 4.5 hours including tutorial and break
No separate exam exists
A clinical skills OSCE administered by ACGME
A guaranteed automatic certificate after fellowship

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPM lists a dedicated Addiction Medicine subspecialty examination and published format. Fellowship completion alone does not automatically certify every trainee; board requirements include other conditions.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which interpretation of a patient's declining psychosocial treatment while seeking MOUD is most appropriate?

options.text: Offer medication treatment and keep the door open to individualized psychosocial supports
Refuse MOUD until the person agrees to therapy
Treat refusal as proof of incapacity
Require residential treatment for all

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC/ASAM-oriented guidance emphasizes patient-centered care and that declining psychosocial treatment or lack of access should not preclude/delay MOUD.

title: Adult Psychiatry Residency
level: Clinical physician residency (independent self-study course; not clinical training)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.level: Advanced medical/graduate self-study for learners with prior biomedical foundations; not a substitute for medical school or supervised clinical training.
expectedKnowledge: Basic anatomy and physiology; neurobiology; general pharmacology and evidence appraisal.
Clinical learner should know this material is educational and should not assess/treat patients independently.
prerequisites.sequence: Units 1–2 establish assessment, development and mechanisms; units 3–10 cover board topic clusters and diagnostic/treatment reasoning; units 11–12 integrate psychotherapy, ethics, law and systems. All units may be sampled by experienced learners.

objectives: Use structured, culturally responsive psychiatric assessment and develop a provisional biopsychosocial-cultural formulation with explicit differential and uncertainty.
Map the current public ABPN primary Psychiatry certification outline across psychiatric disorders and physician competencies/mechanisms.
Critically use public clinical guidelines and source dates without mistaking them for universal mandates.

Explain broad assessment and treatment principles for common psychiatric syndromes, neuropsychiatric and substance-use presentations, and psychotherapy modalities, while identifying when qualified supervised care is necessary.
Apply privacy, consent, ethical and licensing principles when discussing case reports and diagnostic images.
State accurately the distinction between self-study and ACGME training, licensure, clinical competency evaluation and ABPN eligibility.

topicGaps: 21.666389 of the 36 requested video hours remain unfilled by verified, free, unique recordings (14 selected recordings; 51601 observed seconds). Script targets and authored episodes do not reduce this ready-media gap.

Ready recordings are topic-selective grand rounds, not a complete ABPN sequence. There is insufficient ready-video coverage for neurodevelopmental disorders; the full anxiety/OCD/dissociation scope; eating, sexual, gender, elimination, disruptive/impulse-control, and paraphilic disorders; broad neurocognitive/neurologic/sleep disorders and diagnostic procedures; medication classes, special-population cautions, adverse-event emergencies, ECT/rTMS; psychotherapy skills; forensic law; ethics, communication, quality, and systems-based practice.
Some recorded talks are research-focused or exploratory and should be used for mechanism/evidence appraisal only. Their topic titles do not prove guideline-level coverage or clinical recommendations.
All original clip plans and authored episodes are unrendered scripts/plans. The course has no ready original video library and completion of this self-study cannot replace supervised residency.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Scope includes the packet-specified CHA adult physician residency, five exact Harvard Medical School-listed adult psychiatry residencies as institutional variants, and the distinct Johns Hopkins Hospital General Psychiatry Residency. Variants share an adult general-psychiatry board-aligned learning track, not a claim of identical curricula. HMS lists five Harvard adult residencies and names them. Johns Hopkins is a separately described clinical physician residency. Research/postdoctoral fellowships and non-physician training are not counted as residency variants. No combined psychiatry-neurology program was identified in the sources consulted; ABPN permits applying for both specialties after separate qualifying training, not because this is a combined program. Individual current ACGME listing/status was not independently queried for every institution.
sourceCaveats: Current web-access date is 2026-10-07. ACGME cited file is the 2025 reformatted Psychiatry Program Requirements; do not infer that each named program has an independently verified current accreditation status from the general requirement PDF.

HMS officially lists five adult psychiatry residency variants. Some linked institutional pages are dated or did not expose full current details; exact institutional names are preserved and unknown detail remains qualified.
Johns Hopkins officially distinguishes its General Psychiatry Residency from clinical/research postdoctoral fellow listings. The latter are not physician primary-specialty residency tracks.
The ABPN Psychiatry certification examination is a separate primary specialty board assessment. An independent course does not confer eligibility; requirements may change.
A separate combined psychiatry-neurology training program was not verified. Dual ABPN applications can be allowed after separate qualifying training and are not evidence of a single combined program.

Public video playlist listings were not sufficient evidence of playable free lectures with observed durations. Shared YouTube metadata attempts returned rate limiting/403; no bypass/browser-login attempted. Durations remain null/unverified and excluded.

Free-to-view clinical case reports do not grant permission to reuse patient material or images. Links are provided, no patient data/images copied; article-specific licenses/consent must be checked before any reuse.
Clinical guidelines are date- and jurisdiction-specific; they are sources for study, not treatment orders or individualized patient-care advice.

There is insufficient ready-video coverage for neurodevelopmental disorders; the full anxiety/OCD/dissociation scope; eating, sexual, gender, elimination, disruptive/impulse-control, and paraphilic disorders; broad neurocognitive/neurologic/sleep disorders and diagnostic procedures; medication classes, special-population cautions, adverse-event emergencies, ECT/rTMS; psychotherapy skills; forensic law; ethics, communication, quality, and systems-based practice.
Some recorded talks are research-focused or exploratory and should be used for mechanism/evidence appraisal only. Their topic titles do not prove guideline-level coverage or clinical recommendations.

practiceQuestions.stem: An interview reveals several weeks of low mood and poor sleep. Which next move best supports a defensible provisional formulation?

options.text: Record major depressive disorder immediately based only on the two symptoms.
Clarify duration, full symptom pattern, impairment, prior elevated/activated episodes, substances/medications, medical contributors, and safety.
Order an imaging study for every patient with low mood.
Use a symptom scale as a definitive diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Psychiatric assessment integrates course, differential, functional effect and safety. A scale may assist but does not establish diagnosis; testing should be clinically directed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description most clearly distinguishes mania from a brief period of increased productivity?

options.text: Any night of reduced sleep.

A sustained episode of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy/activity and associated symptoms, with clinically significant change from baseline; assess duration, impairment, psychosis, substance/medical causes.
A positive online mood screen.
A family history alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A longitudinal syndrome and differential matter; isolated sleep loss, screening result, or family history alone does not establish mania. Current diagnosis requires application of formal criteria by a qualified clinician.

practiceQuestions.stem: A person reports hearing a voice during a period of heavy stimulant use. Which reasoning is most appropriate?

options.text: Psychotic disorder is established regardless of timing.
Substance-induced psychotic disorder is proven by the report.

Characterize the experience and timeline, assess intoxication/withdrawal and medical causes, obtain collateral when appropriate, evaluate safety, and keep primary psychotic illness in the differential.
No further evaluation is needed if symptoms resolve.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Psychosis has a broad differential. Temporal association raises but does not settle etiology; assess course, substances, medical causes, safety and follow-up.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an appropriate use of the NICE CG178 page in a U.S.-based education course?

options.text: Treat every NICE recommendation as binding U.S. law.
Use it as a free, dated evidence-guidance source, identify it as UK guidance, check the current version and compare local rules and patient context.
Replace individual assessment with the guideline.
Treat a 2014 publication date as proof no later update exists.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current page lists a September 2026 update; it is UK guidance and should not be misrepresented as law or a substitute for individual judgment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best captures the content structure of the ABPN psychiatry certification specification reviewed for this course?

options.text: Only named diagnoses are assessed.
It uses two linked dimensions: psychiatric disorders/topics and physician competencies/mechanisms.
It certifies procedural competence from a video course.
It is an ACGME curriculum.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABPN outline explicitly pairs topic categories with competencies/mechanisms, including treatment, diagnosis, communication and systems practice. It is not ACGME curriculum or a procedure credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: A teaching vignette identifies a person only as a “55-year-old” but reproduces an image from a published case report. What is the right course practice?

options.text: Assume a publicly readable article grants image reuse.
Link to the publication only unless permissions and article-specific licensing/consent have been checked; do not copy or rehost the image.
Remove the age and ignore all copyright.
Use the image if no name appears.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-read is not reuse permission. Link to authentic cases and honor source-specific licensing and consent; do not copy patient images or records.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with opioid use disorder asks about treatment choices. Which response is best for this educational scenario?

options.text: Assert that counseling alone is universally sufficient.

Describe that federal TIP 63 covers methadone, buprenorphine and naltrexone; support individualized shared decision-making and review current clinical/legal requirements with a qualified treatment team.
Tell the patient to abruptly stop all prescribed treatment.
Claim all three medicines have identical initiation rules.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SAMHSA TIP 63 is a source for medication treatment options. Choice and initiation depend on patient-specific factors, product labeling, service setting and current rules; this course gives no treatment orders.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is correct about the public NIDA overdose-prevention video page?

options.text: It is an exhaustive clinical guideline.
The page says video length 4:07 and explicitly notes it is educational and not a guideline or exhaustive procedures review.
It is a complete psychiatry lecture series.
Its duration can be inferred from the playlist average.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NIDA page reports 4:07 and includes explicit limitations. It is a short educational spot, not a full-length lecture; it is not included in counted lecture hours.

practiceQuestions.stem: A course offers 36 hours of planned videos and 4,000 hours of accredited resident rotations; which statement is defensible?

options.text: Both numbers mean this course supplies the same clinical training.
Planned material is not ready video, and even completed videos do not replace the ACGME supervised four-year clinical training program.
The course guarantees ABPN exam eligibility.
Completing videos automatically demonstrates competency.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Plans are not completed recordings and independent media self-study cannot supply supervised clinical experience, accredited training, licensure or board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a question of self-harm risk, what is the safest broad educational principle?

options.text: A score alone precisely predicts individual suicide.
Avoid asking directly because it increases risk.
Assess directly and respectfully in clinical context, use local emergency/safety protocols for imminent danger, and connect people in the U.S. to appropriate crisis help such as 988.
Treat a protective factor as proof of no risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Assessment is contextual and cannot be replaced with a score or single factor. Immediate danger calls for local emergency response; NIMH lists U.S. crisis support at 988.
